patient_has_symptomatic_peripheral_arter.assessment: The patient complains of increasing calf pain with walking (claudication) and has diminished extremity pulses, which directly support a diagnosis of symptomatic peripheral arterial disease.
patient_has_symptomatic_peripheral_arter.evidence: A 72-year-old man complains of increasing calf pain when walking uphill... his lower extremities are slightly cool to the touch and have diminished pulses at the dorsalis pedis.

patient_has_symptomatic_peripheral_arter.evidence: A 72-year-old man complains of increasing calf pain when walking uphill.

There is no mention of critical limb ischemia or of definite >50% infrainguinal stenosis, so this criterion is not met.
